title: WorkOS
intro: What WorkOS offers and its API surface: sign-in, SSO, directory sync, roles, audit logs, and the SDKs.
scope: A summary of what is available and the API, not a replacement for the docs. Prices and plans are left out. WorkOS is a commercial service; the SDKs are open source.

entries.name: What WorkOS is
entries.summary: A hosted API and dashboard that adds enterprise features to a SaaS app: sign-in, SSO, directory sync, roles, audit logs.

sections.title: What you get
items: One REST API at https://api.workos.com, a Dashboard for people who do not code, and SDKs. Each feature below is a product you switch on.
Sign-in: [AuthKit](#authkit) (hosted login, sessions, MFA). Enterprise customers: [SSO](#sso), [Directory Sync](#directory-sync) and the [Admin Portal](#admin-portal) where their IT team sets it up.

Access: [roles and groups](#rbac), [fine-grained authorization](#fga), [feature flags](#feature-flags). Records: [audit logs](#audit-logs), [events and webhooks](#events). Data: [Vault](#vault), [Pipes](#pipes).
Protocols behind SSO and directory sync (SAML, OIDC, SCIM) are in [Identity providers](../identity/index.html).

rows: A staging or production workspace with its own API keys and settings.
A customer of your app. SSO connections, directories and roles hang off it.
A person who signs in through AuthKit. Organization memberships link users to organizations.
One SSO link between an organization and its identity provider.
One synced user directory of an organization, with directory users and groups.

sections.title: Basics
items: Base URL https://api.workos.com. Requests and responses are JSON. Standard HTTP verbs and status codes.
Authenticate with the environment's secret API key as a bearer token: Authorization: Bearer sk_... A missing or wrong key returns 401.
Lists are paginated; see the pagination page for the cursor parameters. Errors have their own reference page.
A testing page explains how to try SSO and directory sync without a real identity provider.

sections.title: Rate limits (the general rule and the exceptions on the page)
items: AuthKit APIs are limited per environment; the page lists them. Over the limit you get 429.

sections.title: What it does
items: A login UI and APIs for users and organization memberships. You redirect to AuthKit, then exchange the returned code for a user and session tokens.
Beyond the login page the API covers email verification, password reset, magic auth, invitations, JWT templates, CORS origins, redirect URIs and API keys for users and organizations.

redirect-uri, create/list CORS origin, JWT template

sections.title: What it is
items: WorkOS publishes SDKs on GitHub, among them Node (workos-node), Python (workos-python), Go (workos-go) and a Next.js AuthKit library (authkit-nextjs). The client libraries page lists the rest.
Each SDK wraps the same REST API; see [API conventions](#api).
